decision: Temporary owner-authorized acceptance for the exact cbc05133 historical Bandit debt and twelve separately reviewed LOW additions. Findings remain reported as debt and are not clean, fixed or accepted for production.

reviewed_additions.reason: Import used only for one shell-free call with fixed absolute runuser and PostgreSQL psql executables; protected passwords stay on stdin and never enter argv.
Absolute runuser and PostgreSQL psql paths, constant flags and a constant SELECT are used; passwords arrive only through stdin and are compared in memory; shell execution is never enabled.
Import supports bounded read-only commands selected exclusively from fixed absolute lsblk, wipefs and systemctl argv; request data cannot select an executable or argument.
The helper is called only with locally authored absolute lsblk and wipefs argv; it bounds output and time, supplies a minimal environment and never enables a shell.
Absolute systemctl path and constant is-active/postgresql.service arguments are used with no external input, bounded output, a timeout and shell disabled.
Import supports bounded shell-free gcloud and Terraform invocations; protected binaries are required to be absolute and version-pinned before use.
INT_PG_APP_PASSWORD is an environment-variable name used to retrieve a protected runtime value; the literal is not credential material and cannot authenticate.
INT_PG_MIGRATOR_PASSWORD is an environment-variable name used to retrieve a protected runtime value; the literal is not credential material and cannot authenticate.
The gcloud path comes from shutil.which, must be absolute, and receives only constant version and format flags in this preflight invocation.

All callers build argv from fixed tools, hard-coded INT resource identities, validated digests and private scratch paths; protected data uses stdin, outputs and time are bounded, and shell is disabled.
Terraform must resolve to an absolute path and is checked against exact version 1.15.8 with constant version argv and a closed CLI configuration before protected use.
Terraform argv uses the pinned binary, reviewed subcommands and private validated plan/module paths; ambient TF options are rejected, output and time are bounded, and shell is disabled.
